status: PRE-REGISTERED — OPEN. Written BEFORE either arm ran; no result exists yet.
param: --weight on the NIGHT and CORPUS composes. One knob. Per-set composes stay unweighted in both arms (their members are equal-depth groups from one sky, where nbstack, unweighted and inverse-variance coincide — a null by construction).

arms.A_historic: --weight=nbstack — what run_corpus_combine.sh defaults to and what run_session_chain.sh:115 hardcodes. This is the incumbent and the control.

pinning: BOTH ARMS COMPOSE THE IDENTICAL MEMBER FILES. The knob lives only in the compose (`stack r_s mean none -norm=addscale [-weight=]`); everything above it — calibrate, undistort, register, group sub-stack — is untouched by it, so rebuilding members per arm would test determinism rather than the knob AND would let upstream variation be attributed to the weighting. Same members, same --framing, same reference, same cull. Everything BELOW the knob (compose, solve, SPCC, render) is fully rerun in both arms.
why_this_is_being_tested: run_undistort_compose.sh derives the inverse-variance weight as n/s^2 and states that nbstack equals it ONLY while every member's per-frame noise s is the same — 'true for members from one night/sky' — and to prefer noise for a MULTI-NIGHT compose. That guidance landed 2026-07-29 (26d57f7). run_corpus_combine.sh, the only multi-night level, was created 2026-08-10 (c808d83) with WEIGHT=nbstack and no stated justification. The default postdates the guidance it contradicts by 12 days, so it is untested rather than deliberate.
hypothesis: Members differ measurably in sky brightness at identical exposure/ISO (2.5 s, ISO 1600, one camera): july31 108-110 ADU against aug06 43-46, aug09 51-57, aug14 49-53 — a 2.56x spread, with the anti-correlated star counts (july31 lowest at 1166-1256, aug06 highest at 1850-1921) that say it is sky and not exposure. Background-limited variance goes as sky, so nbstack over-weights july31's members by up to 2.56x relative to inverse-variance.

quantitative_prediction.value: +5.43% SNR for arm B over arm A on the 4-night corpus combine
quantitative_prediction.computed_over: 77 members / 8,349 frames — july31 17, aug06 13, aug09 22, aug14 25 (aug14's are PREDICTED from post-cull counts; the rest are real STACKCNT headers)
quantitative_prediction.model: sigma_member^2 proportional to sky/n; Var(w) = sum(w^2 sigma^2)/sum(w)^2; nbstack w=n, inverse-variance w=n/sky
assumptions_that_could_break_it: BACKGROUND-LIMITED noise. Read noise is ~3.5 ADU (bgnoise on this session's darks) against 43-110 ADU of sky, so shot noise should dominate — but the gain SHRINKS toward zero as read noise matters more, and this is the assumption most likely to be wrong.
sky is a PROXY for member noise here; siril's -weight=noise uses its own measured member noise, which is the better quantity and may not track sky exactly
aug14's 25 members do not exist yet — their depths are predicted from the post-cull frame counts and the group derivation

instrument: scripts/qa/snr_regions.py — regional SNR (signal-region median minus sky-region median, over the image's own bgnoise), computed WITHIN each stack so -output_norm cancels and the ratio compares across arms. Every measurement is Siril's own (crop + stat + bgnoise); astropy maps the SAME sky boxes into each arm via WCS. Run on the LIKE linear _spcc surfaces of both arms.

decision_rule_fixed_in_advance.WIN: arm B measures >= +3% SNR over arm A, same sign across every region box
decision_rule_fixed_in_advance.NULL: |delta| < 1%, or the sign is inconsistent across boxes — the incumbent stays, and the corpus default is left at nbstack
decision_rule_fixed_in_advance.PARTIAL: +1% to +3% — real but well under prediction; the noise model gets re-examined before anything is adopted
decision_rule_fixed_in_advance.needs-eyes: any change in star shape or colour, which is not what this knob should touch — checked with star_stations + the full-frame lossless finals, never assumed

falsifier: If arm B's SNR is not above arm A's outside measurement scatter, the hypothesis is refuted and nbstack is CORRECT for this corpus — which would itself mean the members are closer to equal-noise than their sky spread implies, and that is a finding worth recording either way.
guard: siril SILENTLY DROPS -weight= under -nonorm (command.c:8759,8763, docs/combine-contract.md section 4). The compose path uses -norm=addscale so it cannot bite, but arm B's siril log will be checked for the weighting line rather than assumed — an unweighted arm B would look exactly like a NULL.

status: AMENDED BEFORE ANY ARM RAN — no measurement of either arm exists yet. Recorded as an amendment rather than edited into the original, so the change is visible.
why_amended: Owner states the longer aug14 sets are deliberate: the objective is to EXTEND the field of view and FILL IN sky that currently has fewer layers stacked. That is a COVERAGE objective, and the original design measured SNR only — which can select the wrong arm for this goal.
the_tension_this_exposes: --weight=noise down-weights july31's members by up to 2.56x. Where many nights overlap deeply that maximises SNR and costs nothing. But in THIN-coverage edge sky — precisely the zones the owner wants filled — a down-weighted contributor reduces EFFECTIVE DEPTH. So the arm that wins on SNR could lose on the stated objective, and the original decision rule would not have detected it.

zone_classes: DEEP OVERLAP — many nights contribute; the knob should show its SNR gain here
THIN EDGE / PARTIAL OVERLAP — few contributors; where the owner's objective lives and where down-weighting can cost depth
SINGLE-NIGHT — one contributor; NEGATIVE CONTROL, the knob must do nothing here, and an effect appearing here voids the result

record_type: NIGHT-LEVEL CONTROL RESULT + instrument refinement, written BEFORE the corpus arms ran

instrument_refinement.what: reading snr_regions.py's per-stack `bgnoise` rather than its headline `snr_per_channel` ratio. SAME instrument, same run, same record — a different field of its output.
instrument_refinement.why: weighting changes NOISE and cannot change SIGNAL: both arms are linear combinations of the SAME members under the same -norm=addscale, so the signal term is identical and the SNR ratio between arms IS the inverse noise ratio. Measuring bgnoise directly estimates the same quantity without dividing by a signal term.
instrument_refinement.why_it_matters_here: MEASURED on this field: the brightest and darkest well-covered 120 px boxes in the linear stack differ by only 1.06x. A (signal-sky)/noise ratio built on 6% contrast is dominated by box choice — my first pair returned NEGATIVE SNR because the nominal 'sky' box was brighter than the nominal 'signal' box. The bgnoise field carries the hypothesis's actual quantity and is not sensitive to box placement.
instrument_refinement.not_a_goalpost_move: recorded BEFORE the corpus arms ran, and it does not change the hypothesis, the arms, the prediction (+5.43%) or the decision thresholds — only which field of the same instrument's output estimates the predicted quantity.

the_prediction_was_WRONG_and_here_is_why.broken_assumption: the pre-registration modelled member variance as proportional to SKY LEVEL (background-limited, sigma ~ sqrt(sky)). It named this as the assumption most likely to fail, but blamed READ NOISE. Read noise is not the reason.
the_prediction_was_WRONG_and_here_is_why.MEASURED_mechanism: members are ALREADY STACKED under -norm=addscale, so normalisation absorbs most of the sky difference BEFORE the compose sees it. Siril bgnoise on real members: july31 2.902-2.938 (green) against aug06 2.406-2.663 — a 1.22x noise spread from a 2.56x SKY spread, where sqrt(sky) predicts 1.60x.
the_prediction_was_WRONG_and_here_is_why.corrected_model: re-running the same variance arithmetic with MEASURED member noise instead of the sky proxy predicts +0.673% — same order as the +0.188% measured, and firmly inside NULL. The residual 0.67 vs 0.19 is within the crudeness of using one member's noise per night as that night's representative.

durable_finding: SKY LEVEL IS NOT A PROXY FOR MEMBER NOISE ON THIS ROUTE. A 2.56x sky spread arrives at the compose as a 1.22x noise spread because every member is a normalised stack. So nbstack and noise are near-equivalent for ANY corpus built this way, and run_undistort_compose.sh's own guidance ('prefer noise for a MULTI-NIGHT compose, where sky brightness differs between members') is TRUE IN PRINCIPLE and IMMATERIAL IN PRACTICE here — the premise it rests on (per-frame noise differing between members) is largely cancelled upstream. That is why run_corpus_combine.sh's nbstack default, which looked like an unreviewed oversight from the commit dates, costs nothing measurable.
what_this_does_NOT_say: it does not show nbstack is CORRECT in general — only that the two are indistinguishable at this corpus's 1.22x member-noise spread. A corpus with genuinely unequal member noise would separate them, and the corrected model is the way to predict whether it is worth testing.
it does not test the OWNER'S coverage objective — depth in thin-edge sky was measured separately and is not a function of this knob at NULL.
